html:
The Bayali are an Aboriginal Australian people of the central Queensland coast around Port Curtis, where the town of Gladstone now stands. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is written about them. Their coastal country gave fish, shellfish, dugong and turtle, with the southern end of the Great Barrier Reef offshore. Neighbours on the map include the Gangulu, the Gureng Gureng and the Darumbal. A short-lived British colony was planned at Port Curtis in 1847, and settlement followed in the 1850s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
